Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:1.hebrew: ולאו קל וחומר הוא - מן הטעם הזה יש לדון דכ"ש לקנין אחר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:1.english: And is it not an a fortiori argument - From this reason one can deduce that [the requirement applies] all the more so to another acquisition.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:2.hebrew: מה גט - דכי איתה בצד חצרה ולא ניחא לה למקנייה, אפילו הכי קנייה לה חצרה, אמרינן דאי איתה — אין, אי לא — לא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:2.english: If [in the case of] a bill of divorce - Where, when she is next to her courtyard and does not want to acquire it, even so her courtyard acquires it for her, [yet] we say that if she is [there] — yes, [and] if not — no.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:3.hebrew: מתנה - דליתה בע"כ, דאי אמרה לא בעינא, לא קניא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:3.english: A gift - For it is not [valid] against her will, as if she says, "I do not want [it]," she does not acquire [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:4.hebrew: לא כ"ש - דכי אמרה בעינא, צריכא שתהא בצד חצרה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:10:4.english: [Is it] not all the more so - That when she says, "I want [it]," she must be beside her courtyard.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:11:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב אשי - לא תתלי טעמא משום דאיתה בעל כרחה, אלא גבי מתנה היינו טעמא דלא בעינן עומד אצלה: דכיון דמידה אתרבאי, לא גרעה משלוחה להיטיב לה. ואילו שלוחה שקיבל לה מתנה, מי לא קני לה ואפילו אין עומדת בצדו? חצרה נמי לא שנא. הלכך, גבי מתנה דזכות הוא לה, אנן סהדי דניחא לה שתהא שלוחה, וקנייא לה כשליח. אבל גבי גט, דחוב הוא לה, לא ניחא לה שתהא שלוחה. הלכך, כי עומדת בצדה, על כרחה ידה היא, וידה קניא גבי גט על כרחה; ואי לא, לאו ידה הוא ולא שלוחה הוא. טעמא דיש חילוק בין גט למתנה, ואף על גב דתרוייהו דעת אחרת מקנה אותן, משום דהך חצר, אף על גב דאתרבאי משום יד כדאמרן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף י:), לא גרעה משליחות, דאי נמי לא אתרבאי מונתן בידה, הוי נפקא לן חצר משליחות; וכי אצטריך לרבויי משום יד, משום קטן וקטנה דלתנהו בתורת שליחות אצטריך. וכל היכא דאיתיה לשליחות, איתיה לדין חצר. הלכך, גבי גט דחוב הוא לה, אין חבין כו', כלומר, אין אדם יכול לעשות שליח לחוב אדם שלא מדעתו, וחצרו נמי לאו בתורת שליחות מצית לאתויי דתתגרש שלא מדעתה. הלכך, בגט לא תרבייה אלא משום יד, ומה ידה דסמוכה לה, אף חצירה בסמוכה לה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:11:1.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said - Do not attribute the reason to [the fact] that it is against her will; rather, regarding a gift, this is the reason that we do not require [her] to be standing beside it: since [a courtyard] was derived from "her hand," it is no worse than her agent for benefiting her. And if her agent received a gift for her, would he not acquire [it] for her even if she is not standing beside him? Her courtyard is also no different. Therefore, regarding a gift, which is a benefit to her, it is presumed that she is pleased for [her courtyard] to be her agent, and it acquires [the gift] for her like an agent. However, regarding a bill of divorce, which is a detriment to her, she is not pleased for [her courtyard] to be her agent. Therefore, when she is standing beside it, against her will it is [considered] her hand, and her hand acquires [it] regarding a bill of divorce against her will; and if not, it is neither her hand nor her agent. The reason there is a distinction between a bill of divorce and a gift — even though in both cases another person's mind transfers ownership — is because this courtyard, even though it was derived as "hand" as we stated above (Bava Metzia 10b), is no worse than agency, for even if it had not been derived from "and he shall place [it] in her hand," we would have derived a courtyard from agency; and when it was necessary to include it as "hand," it was necessary for a minor boy and a minor girl, who are not subject to the law of agency. And wherever agency applies, the law of a courtyard applies. Therefore, regarding a bill of divorce, which is a detriment to her, "one does not act to a person's detriment [in his absence]" etc. — that is to say, a person cannot appoint an agent to act to someone's detriment without his knowledge, and you also cannot bring her courtyard under the law of agency so that she would be divorced without her knowledge. Therefore, regarding a bill of divorce, only include it as "hand": just as her hand is near her, so too her courtyard [only acquires] when it is near her.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:1:1.hebrew: ומקומו מושכר לו - וקבל ממנו שם שכר המקום, דהכי קתני סיפא: נתקבלו זה מזה שכר. וכל כך למה? כדי לקנות מעשר, שתהא חצרו קונה לו, לפי שהמטלטלין אין קונין אלא או במשיכה או חצרו תקנה לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:1:1.english: And its place is rented to him - And he received from him there the rental fee for the place, for thus the latter clause teaches: "They received payment from one another." And why all this? In order to acquire [the] tithe, so that his courtyard would acquire [it] for him, because movable property is acquired only either through pulling [meshikhah], or [by] his courtyard acquiring [it] for him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:1:2.hebrew: נתון לעקיבא - גבאי היה, ואותה שנה שנת מעשר עני היתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:1:2.english: Is given to Akiva - He was a charity collector, and that year was a year of the poor man's tithe.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:4:1.hebrew: כי אתא - ר' אבא לסורא, אמר להו כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:4:1.english: When he came - Rabbi Abba [came] to Sura; he said to them, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:4:2.hebrew: מטלטלי אגב מקרקעי הקנה להם - ולאו משום דתקני להם מקומם בתורת חצר, שאפילו הקנה להן חצר אחרת שאינן בתוכה קנוי נמי, כדתנן (קדושין דף כו.): נכסים שאין להן אחריות נקנין עם נכסים שיש להן אחריות בכסף. משנתן הכסף בשביל הקרקע והמטלטלין, או אפילו קרקע במכר ומטלטלין במתנה, נקנין המטלטלין בקנין הקרקע בלא משיכה, כדילפינן בקדושין (שם) מויתן להם אביהם מתנות רבות לכסף ולזהב עם ערים בצורות אשר ביהודה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:4:2.english: He transferred ownership of movable property to them by means of land - And [this is] not because their place acquires [the produce] for them by virtue of [the law of] a courtyard, for even if he had transferred to them another courtyard in which [the produce] was not [located], [it] would also be acquired, as we learned in a Mishnah (Kiddushin 26a): "Property that does not serve as a guarantee [i.e., movable property] is acquired together with property that serves as a guarantee [i.e., land] through money." Once one has given the money for the land and the movable property — or even [if he acquired] the land by purchase and the movable property as a gift — the movable property is acquired through the acquisition of the land without [an act of] pulling, as we derive in Kiddushin (ibid.) from [the verse], "And their father gave them great gifts of silver and of gold, with fortified cities in Judah."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:1.english: And did they not have a cloth, etc. - Why [did he need] to receive money from them?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:2.hebrew: אלא - סודר מאי טעמא לא? דטובת הנאה שהיתה לו לרבן גמליאל במעשרות הללו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:2.english: Rather - why not [acquire them with] a cloth? Because the benefit of discretion that Rabban Gamliel had in these tithes [is not property].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:3.hebrew: אינה חשובה ממון - דתהא נקנית בחליפין, דליכא למימר כי קנה ליה ר"ג להאי סודר, אקנייה חליפין דידיה בכל מקום שהן, דכיון דאין לו בהן אלא טובת הנאה, שבידו לתתו לכל מי שירצה, אין זו חשובה ממון לחול על זו קנין חליפין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:3.english: It is not considered property - such that it can be acquired by means of exchange, for one cannot say [that] when Rabban Gamliel acquired this cloth, he transferred his [tithes] by exchange wherever they are; for since he has in them only the benefit of discretion, [in] that it is in his power to give it to whomever he wishes, this is not considered property for an acquisition by exchange to take effect upon it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:4.english: Here, too - Regarding the acquisition of land.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:5.hebrew: אינה ממון לקנות על גבי קרקע - בקנין שהקרקע נקנה בו, אלא אפקורי בעלמא אפקר גבייהו. וכי אוגר להו מקום, קנתה לו חצרו בתורת חצר כשאר הפקר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:5:5.english: [It] is not property to be acquired by means of land - With the act of acquisition by which the land is acquired; rather, he merely declared [the tithes] ownerless in their favor. And when he rented them a place, his courtyard acquired [them] for him by the law of a courtyard, like any other ownerless property.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:6:1.hebrew: ולא היא - מהאי דכי לא היה להן סודר, לאו ראיה היא למילף מינה דאין טובת הנאה נקנית בחליפין ועל גבי קרקע, דשפיר איכא למימר מטלטלי אגב קרקעי הקנה להן. ודקשיא לך לקנינהו בחליפין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:6:1.english: But it is not so - From this [argument of] "did they not have a cloth," it is not a proof to learn from it that benefit of discretion is not acquired by means of exchange or by means of land, for one can well say [that] he transferred [ownership] to them [as] movable property by means of land. And [as for] that which is difficult for you, "let him transfer them by means of exchange":

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:6:2.english: Gifts - [Gifts] of the priesthood, of the Levites, and the poor man's tithe.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:6:3.hebrew: נתינה כתיבא בהו - כדכתיב (דברים כ״ו:י״ב): "ונתתה ללוי" — זה מעשר ראשון, "לגר ליתום ולאלמנה" — זה מעשר עני. לפיכך אסור להקנותן בסודר, דדרך מקח הוא, שזה נותן לו כליו תחתיהן ונראה זה כמוכרן לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:6:3.english: Giving is written regarding them - As it is written (Deuteronomy 26:12): "And you shall give [it] to the Levite" — this [refers to] the first tithe; "to the stranger, to the fatherless, and to the widow" — this [refers to] the poor man's tithe. Therefore, it is forbidden to transfer ownership of them by means of a kerchief, for [exchange] is a manner of buying and selling, since this [recipient] gives him his vessel in exchange for them, and this one appears as though he is selling them to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:6:4.english: It is a powerful [form of] giving - It is permitted to transfer ownership of priestly gifts by means of land.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:7:1.hebrew: רב פפא אמר - לעולם בתורת חצר קנאו, ואפילו הכי לא תקשי לעולא. דהא דלא בעינן הכא עומד בצד השדה, משום דדעת אחרת מקנה אותן, שרבן גמליאל הקנה להן מטלטלין שהיו לו בחצר שלהן, ולא מהפקירא קנו. ונוחה מתנה זו לקנות, ואע"ג דאין עומד בצד השדה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:7:1.english: Rav Pappa said - Indeed, they acquired [it] by way of [the law of] a courtyard, and even so it does not pose a difficulty to Ulla. For the reason we do not require here [that the recipient be] standing beside the field is because another mind transfers ownership of them — for Rabban Gamliel transferred to them movable property that he had in their courtyard, and they did not acquire [it] from ownerless property. And this gift is easier to acquire, even though [the recipient] is not standing beside the field.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:8:1.hebrew: והוא שרץ אחריהן - הצבי מהלך והגוזלות מדדין, ומתניתין דקתני זכתה לו שדהו, כגון שהיה יכול לרוץ אחריהן ומגיען קודם שיצאו משדהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:8:1.english: And [this is] provided that he runs after them - The deer is walking and the fledglings are hopping, and [when] the Mishnah teaches "his field has acquired [it] for him," [it refers to] a case where he was able to run after them and reach them before they left his field.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:8:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן ובעי ר' ירמיה במתנה היאך - אם היו צבי וגוזלות של אדם אחד והם בתוך שדה חבירו, ונותנן בעליהן לבעל שדה במתנה, היאך הדין? מי בעינן "והוא שרץ אחריהן ומגיען", ואי לא — לא קני ומצי נותן למיהדר ביה — או לא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:8:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: And Rabbi Yirmeya raises a dilemma: In [the case of] a gift, how [is the law]? - If a deer and young birds belonged to one person and they are inside his fellow's field, and their owner gives them to the owner of the field as a gift, what is the law? Do we require [the condition] "provided that he runs after them and catches them," and if not, he does not acquire [them] and the giver can retract, or not?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:8:3.hebrew: קבלה מיניה רבי אבא - להך בעיא מרבי ירמיה, דשפיר דק שיש חילוק בין מתנה להפקר, ובמתנה אע"פ כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:8:3.english: Rabbi Abba accepted it from him - [He accepted] this dilemma from Rabbi Yirmeya, [agreeing] that he rightly reasoned that there is a distinction between a gift and ownerless property, and regarding a gift, even though [he runs after them and does not reach them], etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:9:1.english: And Ulla says - In Tractate Gittin (77b), regarding one who throws a bill of divorce to his wife into her house or into her courtyard.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 11b:9:2.english: A bill of divorce is different, as it is [effective] against her will - For he gives it to her, and she does not wish [him] to divorce her.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 11b:1:1.hebrew: מקומו מושכר לו - בסיפא קתני שקבלו שכר זה מזה. וא"ת: אמאי קבלו שכר? היה לו להשאיל להם או להשכיר בחליפין! וי"ל: דשאלה ושכירות אינה נקנית בחליפין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 11b:1:1.english: Its place is rented to him - In the latter clause, it teaches that they received payment from one another. And if you ask: why did they receive payment? He could have lent [the place] to them or rented [it] through chalipin [symbolic exchange]! And one can answer: [because] borrowing and renting are not acquired through chalipin.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 11b:2:1.hebrew: וכי בצד שדהו של ר"ג היו עומדין - וא"ת: והלא התבואה היתה בביתו של ר"ג, כדמוכח בירושלמי פרק ג' דמעשרות, וביתו של רבן גמליאל היה משתמר? ויש לומר: דלגבי זקנים לא היה משתמר, שלא היה הפסק בין תבואתו לתבואתן. ואם תאמר: שלהי השואל (לקמן בבא מציעא דף קב.), גבי "הזבל של בעל הבית", מוקי לה בגמרא בתורי דאתו מעלמא ובחצר דמשכיר, וכרבי יוסי בר' חנינא. והשתא, והלא השוכר משתמש בחצר, ואם כן הזבל משתמר לדעת השוכר בחצר, ואיך יזכה המשכיר בזבל תורי דאתו מעלמא? ויש לומר: שגם משכיר ביתו פתוח לאותו חצר, ומקרי עומד בצד שדהו. [וע"ע תוספות גיטין עט: ד"ה פנימית]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 11b:2:1.english: But were [they] standing next to Rabban Gamliel's field - And if you will say: Wasn't the produce in Rabban Gamliel's house, as is proven in the Yerushalmi, chapter 3 of Ma'asrot, and Rabban Gamliel's house was guarded? And one can say: With respect to the elders it was not guarded, because there was no partition between his produce and their produce. And if you will say: At the end of [the chapter] HaSho'el (below, Bava Metzia 102a), regarding "the manure belongs to the homeowner," the Gemara establishes it [as referring] to oxen that come from outside and in the courtyard of the landlord, and in accordance with Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Chanina. Now, doesn't the tenant use the courtyard, and if so, the manure is guarded with the tenant's knowledge in the courtyard — so how does the landlord acquire the manure of oxen that come from outside? And one can say: The landlord's house also opens onto that same courtyard, so he is called "standing next to his field." [And see also Tosafot, Gittin 79b, s.v. penimit].
